Why gold?
There was a time when one troy ounce of gold cost just $20. Today its price is above $3,400. Despite fluctuations, gold has shown steady growth for decades and is widely used as a hedge against inflation. On top of that, it’s a limited resource — scarcity helps preserve its value. 📊
Do you need to store gold physically?
Not anymore. In the past, gold was available only in bars or coins. Now there’s a new format — digital gold. Tether (the creators of digital dollar USDT) launched the XAUT token, pegged to physical gold. Each token equals one troy ounce of gold, backed by real reserves stored securely in Switzerland.
In Crypto Wallet, XAUT is simply called Gold. 🍫
Digital Gold keeps all the advantages of the classic metal: long-term growth, further protection against inflation and global recognition — while offering the flexibility of crypto.

Gold remains one of the few assets investors use to preserve value:

● Limited supply. Gold reserves are finite, and global production grows by just about 1% per year. In total, around 220,000 tons of gold have been mined throughout history.

😱 A stranger messaged you? Here’s what it might lead to
Sometimes scams don’t start with a phishing link — they begin with a simple, friendly, or even “accidental” message from a stranger. This is how many social-engineering schemes work: the scammer gains your trust first, only to later try to take your money or access your accounts.
Recently our support team handled several such cases, and we want to share how these schemes unfold so you can avoid losing your funds.
Scammers usually look for victims in Telegram groups about investments or crypto. They study your messages and behavior in the chat to understand how best to approach you. Then an unknown account (often posing as the opposite gender) writes to you “by mistake”. The stranger tries to get closer emotionally: sharing personal stories, asking questions, showing empathy — building trust over days or even weeks 😎
Once the connection is established, they suddenly tell you about a “great earning opportunity” — a website or app where you can supposedly make quick money with little effort. These fake sites often imitate well-known brands, making the scheme more convincing 🧙
They will ask you to deposit a small amount to “test the service”. Sometimes scammers even allow you to withdraw a tiny profit at the start to help build confidence. However, they will keep asking you to make deposits, and will stop you from withdrawing — saying that you need to wait or must first pay a commission or “fee” to the platform. At this point, it’s already too late: the site is fake, your funds were sent to the scammers’ wallets, and withdrawals are impossible.
🛡 How to protect yourself
If you’ve already sent money to scammers, recovering it is usually impossible. That’s why prevention is key:
● Don’t trust strangers who offer “easy profit” — this is always a scam.
● Never send crypto to external sites, services or apps just because someone in private messages told you to. Especially if they ask you to “top up your trading balance” or pay a “withdrawal fee”.
● If one of your contacts randomly asks you to send them money or use an external service, always double-check that it’s really them — and not an impersonator who hacked their account.
Following these simple rules significantly reduces the risk of losing your funds 🎉

💪 How to set financial goals
A new year often comes with plans and promises to yourself — including financial ones. One key skill can help you achieve success: knowing how to set clear financial goals. When goals are specific, it becomes easier to understand how much you need to earn or save and how long it will take.
For example, you can build your financial goals using the SMART framework (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound):
● Specific
Not just “save money,” but “save $3,000 for home repairs”.
● Measurable
So you can track progress over time.
● Achievable
Realistic and aligned with your income and expenses.
● Relevant
Connected to something that truly matters to you.
● Time-bound
A goal should have a clear deadline or timeframe.
For example, a goal to save $20,000 for a car in two years means about $830 per month. With a monthly income of around $2,500, this would require setting aside roughly 33% of your income. That’s significant, but achievable with proper planning. If needed, the goal could be adjusted — by extending the timeframe or by incorporating investments instead of savings alone.
The key is to stay honest with yourself. Unrealistic goals can be more discouraging than market volatility. When you plan your finances, you’re really planning your life 👩

🧙 What to know before buying crypto
Cryptocurrency attracts people with its opportunities and success stories, but also requires careful thinking. Before buying, it’s important to pause and ask yourself a few simple questions to avoid unnecessary risks and disappointment.
● Why do you want crypto
Are you saving for a long-term goal, exploring a new technology, or hoping to benefit from price growth? Understanding your motivation helps you stay rational and avoid emotional, impulsive decisions.
● Be prepared for volatility
Crypto prices can change significantly in a short period of time — both up and down. Define your investment horizon in advance.
● Don’t put everything into one asset
Avoid investing all your funds in a single asset, even if it looks especially promising. Spread your funds across different assets and use only the amount you can afford to lose without impacting your finances.
● Take care of security
Blockchain transactions are irreversible, so attention to detail matters. Always double-check addresses before sending, make smaller test transactions and avoid suspicious links.
● Consider taxes and regulations
Crypto transactions may be subject to taxes depending on your country. It’s best to understand local rules in advance and keep a record of your transactions.
The main rule: invest only what you can afford to lose without affecting your everyday life . Start small, learn as you go and move at a pace that feels comfortable for you 👩

🧙 Spot vs Perpetuals: what’s the difference?
Crypto Wallet offers two trading tools: spot trading and perpetuals. Here’s how they differ.
🔃 Spot means you buy and own the asset. You purchase a token (e.g. BTC or ETH) and it appears in your balance. You can hold it, send it or sell it at any time.
📈 Perpetuals let you trade price movements without owning the asset. You can open positions: Long — if you expect the price to rise; Short — if you expect the price to fall.
Think of it as trading the direction of price, not the asset itself. If the market moves in your favor — you may make profit. If not — the position may result in a loss.
💪 Key difference: leverage
Spot trading uses only your own funds. Perpetuals allow you to trade a larger position using leverage . Part of your funds is used as margin to control a bigger position.
In Crypto Wallet, leverage is available up to 50x. You can start with as little as $1.
Even small price movements can significantly impact the result when using leverage. If the market moves against your position, it may be liquidated — automatically closed.
👩 Crypto Wallet uses isolated margin — you risk the amount allocated to the position. If liquidation happens, other assets in your wallet are not affected.
Both tools are available directly inside Telegram. Your choice depends on your strategy and how you manage risk.

A common beginner mistake in trading
One of the most frequent causes of losses is having no exit plan. Traders open positions, the price moves against them, and they close with a bigger loss than originally intended. Emotions get in the way — and there's no clear plan to fall back on.
Two tools can help solve this: stop-loss and take-profit.
🫴 Stop-loss — a price level at which your position closes automatically to limit further loss if the market moves against you.
📈 Take-profit — a price level at which your position closes automatically once your target is reached. It lets you lock in gains without watching the chart constantly.
💳 Together, they form a trade plan : you define your maximum acceptable loss and your profit target in advance, and execution happens automatically when those levels are reached.
In Crypto Wallet, both levels can be set when opening a position, or adjusted afterwards in the Perpetuals section.
Open Crypto Wallet and try it on your next trade — a small habit that makes a big difference.

🥸 Crypto phishing: how to stay safe
Scammers impersonate trusted sources to steal your data or money. In crypto, it's especially dangerous — transactions can't be reversed.

1⃣ Fake website
You search for Wallet on Google, click the first link, and land on a clone. The address looks almost real, but something's off: wa1let tg, wall3t-tg, etc. You enter your details and they go straight to scammers.

2⃣ Fake bot
A bot called "Wallet Support" messages you asking to verify your account or share a code. It looks convincing: icon, description, even reviews.
How to check: there's only one official support bot @wallet_supportbot . No others exist.
3⃣ Message from "the team"
"Your account is blocked", "Verify your identity immediately", "You've won a prize." The goal is always the same: get you to click a link or hand over your details.
How to check: Wallet Support never messages first and never asks for codes. All official communications come through verified social channels or the mini app.
💡 The golden rule: verify the source before entering anything. And keep our official channels handy so you always know where the real Wallet is.
